gaps: Linked evidence proves declaration typing and provider lifecycle, native publication on both server hosts, and browser publication removal/reenable through the same recipe. Chromium and Firefox custom/reference renderers now have native actions, error feedback, unmount/remount, replacement, dependency-loss and host-close evidence. Firefox delayed-response replacement and global page-error capture, full surface placement, catalog compatibility, self-accepting renderer replacement and every supported preview failure case remain separate obligations. Native CSS HMR, renderer-module page reload and invalid-source recovery now have maintained real Chromium/Firefox development evidence on both native server hosts; they preserve backend/provider state and native form behavior.

A view setup recipe registers owned cleanup explicitly through its activation scope. Structural JavaScript return values are not adopted. Transform registration uses the same native setup contract; complete native transformation mechanisms and failure cases remain separate work. Script registration now has its own native setup contract and evidence group.

The response-inspector proof links the exact shared JSON spec/actions, reference/custom rendering, mount-local callbacks, peer projections and real owned response/marker effects across both native server hosts and packaged Chromium/Firefox extensions. Both browsers now verify one panel with all three native providers, realm/provider selection, independent state and isolated disconnect; Chromium configuration returns a partial rejection while Firefox succeeds on all providers. Real HTTP failure/recovery runs on both browsers and both server renderers. Eight native preview tests verify response changes/reset, marker rejection before state/HTML mutation and independent resource disposal. Packed contracts compile and execute separately; the installed native artifact consumer now composes packed actions and view publication/state/disposal on both context types in Bundler and NodeNext, without claiming browser mounting or HTTP effects. Packed browser/native host I/O composition, extension error recovery, broader inspector development/reload transitions, cancellation races and an optional CDB profile remain open. Standalone mixed hosts use public initHub origin/auth options; the native Vite wrapper is not covered by that composition. Firefox Classic receipts claim visible-state checks, not global error capture. Extension custom rendering now has Chrome/Firefox native broadcast, replacement and disconnect evidence. Chrome/Firefox watched inspector production proofs now cover both native preview hosts, reference/custom actions, failed-build retention, recovery and close; existing documents do not automatically reload.

Chrome/Firefox pinned inspector caller-disconnect proofs observe native sender socket closure, one completed held HTTP request, unchanged provider incarnation and alternate host, and retained state at observer/remount. They configure no available fallback selector and do not inspect the abandoned Promise, promise backend cancellation/rollback, or cover extension/preview races.

gaps: The common API owns native registration and cleanup. Bounded Vite HTML, native Chromium/Firefox DNR header and same-origin redirect examples, and Firefox byte-stream filtering establish their own timing, independent lifecycle and native failures in supported development/production modes. Chromium explicitly rejects the unavailable Firefox filtering method. No common response pipeline or cross-mechanism order is claimed.

Firefox server execution, frames/CSP, permission revocation, rule limits, native cleanup failure, worker/restart restoration, persistent response-listener wakeup and brotli/zstd, malformed/truncated encodings, range responses, caching and HTTP/2/3 still need exact native evidence. Admitted Firefox stream completion after disposal is covered. Firefox WebDriver Classic lacks global page-error capture. Native mechanisms retain their own outcomes. Valid gzip/deflate with fixed-length and chunked framing now have exact delivered-byte/header evidence in both Firefox modes; original encoded headers remain visible, with no SDK header-normalization promise.

Running-background Firefox loopback streams now have distinct native reader-cancellation and Fetch-abort evidence in production and development. Reader cancellation is a bounded consumption observation, not an upstream cancellation guarantee; Fetch abort reaches native onstop without a filter error. Page destruction, other consumers, cancellation with other encodings/protocols and idle wakeup remain unproved. No SDK cancellation policy is inferred.

The response-inspector proof links the exact shared JSON spec/actions, reference/custom rendering, mount-local callbacks, peer projections and real owned response/marker effects across both native server hosts and packaged Chromium/Firefox extensions. Both browsers now verify one panel with all three native providers, realm/provider selection, independent state and isolated disconnect; Chromium configuration returns a partial rejection while Firefox succeeds on all providers. Real HTTP failure/recovery runs on both browsers and both server renderers. Eight native preview tests verify response changes/reset, marker rejection before state/HTML mutation and independent resource disposal. Packed contracts compile and execute separately; the installed native artifact consumer now composes packed actions and view publication/state/disposal on both context types in Bundler and NodeNext, without claiming browser mounting or HTTP effects. Packed browser/native host I/O composition, extension error recovery, broader inspector development/reload transitions, cancellation races and an optional CDB profile remain open. Standalone mixed hosts use public initHub origin/auth options; the native Vite wrapper is not covered by that composition. Firefox Classic receipts claim visible-state checks, not global error capture. Extension custom rendering now has Chrome/Firefox native broadcast, replacement and disconnect evidence. Chrome/Firefox watched inspector production proofs now cover both native preview hosts, reference/custom actions, failed-build retention, recovery and close; existing documents do not automatically reload.
